rule: The locked final test evaluated three models on two endpoints. It did not evaluate the paired regime contrasts H1-H4 require, so no hypothesis is marked as retested there.

H1.original_definition: Adding target-station PM2.5 history (R0 -> R1) improves macro station-horizon MAE.
H1.why_not_retested: B3_R0 and B3_R1 were not authorized final-test models.
H1.limitations: A single paired contrast on one model family, measured before the test was opened.
H1.permitted_wording: Target PM2.5 history substantially improved development validation accuracy.

H2.hypothesis: The benefit of PM2.5 history is largest at short horizons.
H2.original_definition: The R0 -> R1 gain decreases as forecast horizon grows.
H2.why_not_retested: No R0/R1 pair was evaluated on the locked test.
H2.limitations: Locked-test horizon results are consistent with the pattern but are not a paired contrast and do not test it.
H2.permitted_wording: On development validation the benefit of target history was largest at the shortest horizon and diminished with lead time.
H2.prohibited_wording: The final test confirmed the horizon-dependent benefit.

H3.hypothesis: Co-pollutant history provides additional predictive value.
H3.original_definition: Adding co-pollutant history (R1 -> R2) improves macro station-horizon MAE.

evidence.note: Positive means the R2 variant improved. Only the gradient-boosted family improved; all three learned families degraded.

H3.why_not_retested: Only B3_R2 was evaluated on the locked test, so no R1/R2 contrast exists there.
H3.limitations: The direction of the effect depends on model family; it was positive only for gradient boosting.
H3.permitted_wording: Co-pollutant history helped the gradient-boosted model on development validation and degraded the neural and transformer variants.

H4.hypothesis: Cross-station information provides additional predictive value.
H4.original_definition: A cross-station regime (R3) improves on the same architecture without it (R2).
H4.status: ROBUSTLY SUPPORTED ON DEVELOPMENT / ROBUSTNESS EVIDENCE, BUT NOT INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED ON THE LOCKED TEST
H4.why_not_retested: SA_R2 and SA_R3 were excluded from the confirmatory set.
H4.limitations: The h=24 effect was not reliably directional across seeds. Phase-7 spatial diagnostics found no proximity effect: Spearman(distance, attention) = 0.136289.
H4.permitted_wording: Cross-station context improved the same architecture in a paired comparison across all five seeds on development validation.
H4.prohibited_wording: Geographic propagation, spatial reasoning, distance-driven attention, or confirmation on the final test.

H5.hypothesis: Modern and spatiotemporal methods reduce severe-tail error and under-prediction.
H5.original_definition: Sequence and cross-station models improve severe MAE relative to engineered and naive baselines.
H5.status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED AGAINST SOME LEARNED AND ENGINEERED MODELS, BUT NOT SUPPORTED AS SUPERIORITY OVER PERSISTENCE ON THE LOCKED TEST
H5.locked_test_note: GRU_R1 and B3_R2 both carried confirmatory roles, so the GRU_R1 vs B3_R2 severe comparison is measurable on the locked test. The hypothesis as originally framed concerns a model class rather than these two artifacts, and the class-level contrast was not retested.
H5.limitations: The reference persistence benchmark had the lowest severe MAE on the locked test. Phase-7 showed severe-tail metrics swinging 29-35 ug/m3 across seeds, and the evaluated GRU artifact is a single seed.
H5.permitted_wording: On the locked test GRU_R1 achieved a lower severe MAE than B3_R2, while persistence remained the strongest severe benchmark.
H5.prohibited_wording: The severe-tail problem is addressed; GRU beats persistence in severe pollution; H5 is confirmed.
